variant.title: Minimal — the cut, simple: fixed lights only
variant.summary: No stage, no towers: the DJ stand alone, the crane parked over it. THE CUT — one straight 12 m line sloped 15° under the bridge, low house left, high over the press — on 3 bridled hoists with tie-offs, lit ONLY by what the rental house has that does not move: a curtain of 7 COB200 straight down, an X of 6 PL5403 crossing over the DJ, 4 red PL5403 grazing the bridge; 6 PL5403 pillars at the column bases, 8 red column uplights, 3 on the press; 2 hazers. No moving heads, no strobes.

The rental house's own datasheets are still OWED to confirm.

provenance.hall: scripts/place/rigs/moxir-hall-dims-2026-09-28.json (flat space-frame roof, 4 spans x 24 m, 18 bays; photos + 2020 satellite) + moxir-hall-features-2026-09-28.json (the owner's zones marked 2026-09-28, the press massing, gates, cranes; sizes estimated).
provenance.models: Fixture bodies are the models in scripts/place/fixtures/glb, built to the datasheet dimensions by scripts/place/fixtures/build_fixtures.py (see the manifest for provenance and licence).
provenance.stage: The owner, 2026-09-28, on the first rebuild: "i mention the dj place i think it will not big how you created you made it so big, so stage is the near the metal thing like dj near a bit top and centre of the metal things". So the 'stage' is a DJ place: a small riser, a bit raised, centred on the forging press ('the metal things'), close in front of it; the machinery is the picture behind the DJ. Positions from the photographs (photo 032's fitted camera, cross-checked from photo 004 with EXIF intrinsics; scripts/place/photo_meta.py).
provenance.versions: scripts/place/rigs/moxir-versions-2026-10-17.json: 2026-09-28, on /moxir: "make 3 version with the full, midle, and simple minimalistic and also look to moxir mood, set, vibe and its the undegroudn rave thing lights like that not the commercial shit"

assumptions: The DJ place (the owner's green, 2026-09-28) is a riser of stage decks 3 m wide x 2 m deep x 1.2 m high ON THE NAVE CENTRE LINE (x 0; the owner, 04:13: 'make the scene in center'), its back edge 1.0 m in front of the press's face (z 3.2 m, +-1.5 m), facing the entry and the crowd. The press stays where it stands, 1.65 m right of the axis (range 0.5-3.5), behind the right half of the riser. Three 2 x 1 m decks on 1.2 m legs; 'a bit top' read as 1.0-1.4 m. Options considered: stage.options (D chosen).

The DJ stands behind a 1.8 x 0.8 m DJ table, 0.95 m high, at the riser's front edge; treads up the left side (toward the backstage); a crowd barrier 1.3 m in front of the riser, 9 m long. The crowd (blue) fills the floor from the barrier to under the crane.

The machinery stays the backdrop: the press (to 5.3 m) stands behind the right half of the riser and the machine line beside it further right, so from the floor the DJ is seen against the press; the goalpost header at 7 m is above the press's crown.

No stage deck, no towers: the DJ stand alone. THE CUT: one straight 12 m line of 290 mm square box truss, planned on the Prolyte H30V (4 × H30V-L300; the rental house's own truss and its load table owed), sloped 15° in the bridge's plane — bottom chord 3.44 m at house left (x -6.04) to 6.55 m at house right (x 5.55) — on 3 bridled chain hoists at their shortest drop, with safety steels and a tie-off at each end; load on the line ≈ 203 kg, 39 / 114 / 50 kg a pick (house left → right, ESTIMATE). rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels).

Strobes, blinders and hazers are other-supplier lines (the rental house lists none): each is a planning type modelled on a named product (scripts/place/fixtures/fixtures.json, EXT- codes). No CO2 jet, cold spark or confetti — the underground brief (versions file, method).

Each LOOK is one static state for previsualisation (a focus palette), not a show: positions are the rig's, aims and colours the look's. Every lamp but the press's own six mirrors about the nave centre line (x 0), the booth's axis too. Brightness between fixtures follows the datasheets (photometry below); the overall exposure is one chosen number (photometry.sceneScale).

truss.section_class: 290 mm square box truss, planned on the Prolyte H30V (4 × H30V-L300; the rental house's own truss and its load table owed)
truss.slope_why: the steepest slope the brief's two ends allow together: the high end is capped by the bridle at the high pick (below), the low end kept ≈ 3.5 m; 15° is the brief's floor for reading as a deliberate slash, not a sag
truss.x_offset_why: the line runs u −6.25…+5.75 along itself (x −6.04…+5.55): a clamp point every 0.5 m, 0.25 m in from each end (src/rigbuild/pieces.js), then falls on the DJ's axis, so every lamp stands on a clamp point and the centre beam sits over the DJ
truss.trim_at: trim_m (derived) is the bottom chord at u = 0, over the DJ's axis, measured vertically; the high pick sets it (versions.mjs craneCut)
truss.why: The owner's pick, 2026-09-29: option 4 of ~/Downloads/moxir-crane-rig/ten-truss.html (also https://dev.diiii.xyz/moxir/p/moxir-truss) — 'the cut': ONE straight 12 m truss in the vertical plane right under the yellow crane bridge, LOW house left (−x), HIGH house right (+x, over the forging press and the machine line). Chosen for being epic AND easy: a plain straight truss, 3 hanging points, nothing on the floor. It replaces Minimal's 8 m flat line (x −4.25…3.75, bottom chord 6.0 m, 2 hoists).
truss.trim_why: derived (versions.mjs craneCut): the high pick's bridle at its 120° limit puts its apex at 7.57 m; the hoist's shortest drop under it (0.85 m) and the chords at that pick leave 5.06 m for the bottom chord over the axis

rigging.picks_why: 3 picks: 0.5 m in from each end and one near the middle (u −0.5: between the centre beam and its neighbour, so no beam rises through a bridle or a chain); spans 5.25 and 5.75 m — well inside the H30V's table (Prolyte: 6 m span, uniformly distributed 321.6 kg/m allowable)
rigging.hoist: chain hoist 500 kg, D8 Plus (planned on the CHAINMASTER D8Plus Ultra 500 kg SK030/76U; the rental house's hoists owed)
rigging.hoist_kg_source: CHAINMASTER product data sheet DS_CH_D8PLUS_SK_030-76U_500kg_4m_1f-400V-50Hz_DC.pdf rev 1.1 (18.10.2024) §2.2: 'Weight (without chain): approx. 20 kg' incl. suspension plate, hook tackle, direct control — https://chainmaster.de/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/DS_CH_D8PLUS_SK_030-76U_500kg_4m_1f-400V-50Hz_DC.pdf
rigging.chain_kg_per_m_source: same data sheet §2.2: 'Weight of the chain: approx. 0.59 kg/m' (P5.4 × 15 mm, EN 818-7)
rigging.chain_carried_why: ESTIMATE: a hoist carries its whole chain (in the bag) whatever the drop; 12 m assumed until the rental house's hoists are known

drop.why: the SHORTEST drop the hoist allows: the hoist hangs straight from the bridle apex and is run up to its top at trim, so what swings under the apex is only the hoist itself

stack_m.basis: ESTIMATE (a 3.25 t bow shackle's inside length is ~60 mm)

stack_m.what: hoist, suspension plate hole to hook bottom at the shortest chain
stack_m.basis: CHAINMASTER SK030/76U dimension sheet (same PDF, §3.1/§3.2): suspension plate 97 + body 192 + chain exit 28 + hook tackle 227 mm — summed from the drawing (the maker states no single headroom figure)

stack_m.what: round sling, basket hitch over both top chords, on the hook

stack_m.basis: so the hoist never runs onto its upper limit at trim

bridle.what: each pick a two-leg bridle (a V) from the TWO girders of the bridge, apex over the line, the hoist under the apex — not one vertical chain: the V fixes the pick across the bridge (z)
bridle.attach: a girder beam clamp on the INNER edge of each girder's bottom flange (the girders' inner faces are 1.5 m apart: hall.json cranes girders_dz ±1.1, girder_w 0.7), a shackle, a steel leg to the apex
bridle.clamp_drop_basis: ESTIMATE: girder clamp jaw + shackle under the flange
bridle.max_included_why: the entertainment-rigging limit on a two-leg bridle (at 120° each leg carries the whole load; beyond, more than it): H. Donovan, Entertainment Rigging (2002), bridle tension tables — the high pick is designed AT it, the others far inside
bridle.hardware_basis: ESTIMATE: two girder clamps, two steels, shackles and ring per pick

rigging.safety: a secondary safety steel at every pick from the top chords to its OWN clamp on the back girder, independent of bridle and hoist (DGUV Vorschrift 17/18, BGV C1 practice: a secondary suspension for every load over people)

tieoffs.what: house-left end to the nave column at x −11.6 (inner face) on grid line z 6.0, at the end's own height — a 2 t LC ratchet strap (EN 12195-2) or a 6 mm steel with a turnbuckle
house-right end down to the nave column at x +11.6 on grid line z 6.0, at 5.5 m — under the crane runway beam (6.56–7.46 m on the column line); same strap or steel

rigging.tieoffs_why: the V bridles hold the line across the bridge; ALONG the line (x) each V still swings from its leg tops, and slings on a sloped chord want to creep downhill. Two opposed tie-offs, tensioned against each other (hand-tight, ~50 daN, ESTIMATE), hold it along x; each sling is choked against a node (a vertical brace) so it cannot slide down the slope (Prolyte user manual: loads applied at the nodes).
rigging.truss_kg_per_m_source: Prolyte H30V standard lengths table: H30V-L300 3.00 m 18.90 kg (https://www.prolyte.com/products/aluminium-truss/square-truss/h30v-l100-square-30-length-100-cm, read 2026-09-29) → 6.3 kg/m
rigging.extras_basis: clamps, safety bonds and the cable loom along the line: +10 % of the lamps — ESTIMATE
rigging.crane: the nave's entry-end bridge crane, rolled along its runway to park over the DJ (bridge centre line z 4.8, girder bottom 8.15 m — ESTIMATED; rail 7.6 m, range 6.6–8.4)
rigging.signoff: rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels): the crane's rated load, a check of the old runway, rails and brakes; the crane locked in place and its power isolated for the whole event; bridle, tie-offs and safety steels to a rigger's plan with point loads, signed by a structural or rigging engineer; load cells on the three hoists at trim (a 3-point line is statically indeterminate: the middle pick's share moves with the chains' lengths). This file draws it; they approve it.

load.truss_basis: Prolyte H30V standard lengths table: H30V-L300 3.00 m 18.90 kg (https://www.prolyte.com/products/aluminium-truss/square-truss/h30v-l100-square-30-length-100-cm, read 2026-09-29) → 6.3 kg/m
load.extras_basis: clamps, safety bonds and the cable loom along the line: +10 % of the lamps — ESTIMATE
load.method: a continuous beam on three supports (flexibility method, versions.mjs threePointReactions), the lamps as point loads at their places, the truss as a uniform load; the hoist (datasheet 20 kg), its chain (0.59 kg/m × the chain carried) and the bridle hardware load the bridge on top (picks[].on_bridge_kg); leg tension = on-bridge load / (2 cos(half the included angle)). ESTIMATE, static, before any dynamic factor.
load.note: a 3-point line is statically indeterminate: this split holds for three hoists at one trim; the middle pick's share moves with the chains' lengths — load cells at trim. rigging sign-off owed (crane rated load, lock-out, hoists + safety steels).

clearance.note: the line hangs in the bridge's plane (z 4.8), behind the crowd barrier: no audience stands under it; the low end is over the back of house-left

motion.min_move_why: the owner's rule (2026-09-29): moving heads on a chain-hung line must not swing it — no full-range pan/tilt faster than 4 s, i.e. a cue that moves a head on the line fades in 4 s or more
motion.resonance_why: no periodic pan/tilt effect whose period lies within ±25 % of any natural period of the hang (method written down here, unvalidated: a common resonance-avoidance margin — machine foundations are kept ±20 % away; we take 25 %). Periods: T = 2π√(L/g), L the pendulum length (versions.mjs craneCut)

par.angleNote: the UP-PL5403's standard 15 deg lens (source D); candela scaled from the equivalent's 25 deg figure

cob200.class: 200 W COB PAR, warm + cool white (the rental house's own)
cob200.angleNote: 45° — the narrower of its two lenses (60°/45°, the maker's listing), so a row of them reads as a sheet in haze

groups.note: THE CURTAIN: 7 COB200 hung under the middle 6 m of the cut (u 0, ±1, ±2, ±3 — a metre apart), straight down: in haze a sheet of white whose top edge IS the slope; strobing (the unit strobes 1–25 /s) it is the hit. Fixed focus — the same aim in every look.

THE X: 3 PL5403 hung under each end (u ±4, ±4.5, ±5), all focused on one point 1 m over the DJ's head (x 0, 4.0 m, in the bridge's plane): the low left three rise into it, the high right three fall into it, and they cross — MOXIR's X over the DJ. Hung, not standing: standing on a 15° chord their beams would run through the truss. Fixed focus.
4 PL5403 standing on the cut (u ±2, ±3.5), grazing the underside of the bridge's audience-side girder outward in deep red — the crane drawn as a frame (kept from the flat line). Fixed focus.

6 PL5403 at the bases of every other nave column pair (z 12, 24, 36), straight up into the space frame — the fixed-light version of the column beams (a 15° PAR's column in haze, not a 380 W beam's rod). Fixed focus.
8 PARs up the inner faces of the OTHER column pairs (z 6, 18, 30, 42): beam, red column, beam, red column down the nave — the structure revealed in pieces

3 PL5403 at the press's foot, on the backdrop line's clamp points (x 0.5, 1.5, 2.5 — 0.55/1.65/2.75 fell between them, so no look ever reached them: RIG_BUILD §19.4). The press rises out of the dark in the blade and the red room.

effects.label: hazer
effects.note: 2 hazers on the floor behind the line, either side of the booth: the haze rolls from behind the DJ over the floor

budget.why: A browser cannot run ~90 real three.js spot lights: each is a term in the shader of every lit pixel and, with shadows on, a shadow render and a texture unit each (WebGL gives 16-32; past that every lit material fails to compile). Every fixture draws its beam cone; only these 8 lamps also light the room (the rest of the PARs' light on the columns and the press is baked, wash-glb.mjs), and shadows are OFF by default (the owner found the first version too laggy, 2026-09-27). Measured — see scripts/place/README.md, 'The rig'.
budget.realNote: 2026-09-28 (DJ place): the press's own uplights stand 0.35 m from it, where a real lamp in the renderer blows the face out white; they are baked like the other PARs, and the 4 header spots (6.3 m up, over the DJ and the press) are the real lamps that light the backdrop.

night.note: Darker than the base's readable night (ambient 0.8 -> 0.5, directional 0.35 -> 0.22): darkness is part of the design here (rule 1); the hall must still read in a render. Tuned by eye on the RTX 3080, 2026-09-28.

photometry.method: scripts/place/rig-lib.mjs, 'PHOTOMETRY': candela from the manifest (I = E*d^2 from a measured illuminance, else I = flux / beam solid angle); zoom keeps flux; three.js SpotLight intensity is candela x sceneScale; beam-in-air brightness ~ I*tan(theta/2), scaled to the brightest class, Stevens exponent 1/3, times `air`.
photometry.sceneScaleNote: ONE exposure number for the whole rig, chosen so the room reads in a browser's tone mapping (ACES, exposure 1). The ratios between fixtures are the datasheets'.
photometry.airNote: how much haze is in the air: the brightest class's beam gets this `haze` (0..1, src/objectComponents/spotBeam.js).
photometry.airWhy: Heavy haze (rule 4; 2-6 hazers in every version where the base had 4 smoke machines): every cone's air brightness at 1.5 where the base rig draws 0.9. A drawing choice, not photometry — the ratios between the fixtures stay the datasheets'.

white-cathedral.title: White cathedral + the X
white-cathedral.intent: The nave of cold white pillars from the column bases into the roof, and the X: three PARs from each end of the cut crossing a metre over the DJ's head. Everything else dark.

red-room.title: Red room
red-room.intent: Deep red only: the columns, the press at full and the bridge frame; the cut itself dark, a black slash across the red.

strobe-hit.title: The hit
strobe-hit.intent: The peak: the curtain and the X at full white on black (the COBs' own strobe on a console), everything else out.

one-beam.title: Blackout + one shaft
one-beam.intent: Everything out but one: the curtain's centre COB straight down on the DJ — a shaft of white in the haze, the DJ inside it.

slow-sweep.title: The blade
slow-sweep.intent: The curtain on: seven COBs straight down under the cut, a sheet of white whose top edge is the slope; the bridge a low red frame, the columns and the press glowing up out of the dark in red.

opening.note: the first screen of the crane rig: 14 m out on the dance floor, on the centre line, eye height, looking up to 5.2 m so the crane bridge and the line hung under it frame the DJ, the press glowing behind (tuned by looking, 2026-09-28 night: at 20 m / 4.6 m the bridge read small over an empty floor)
